title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with Police
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with Police] What should I do if a cop stops me while I'm flyering?

Karl's answer: Keep your cool and ask if you are free to go; if they say yes, walk away immediately. If you're detained, state clearly that you are exercising your right to remain silent and refuse any searches of your bag or phone. Don't try to win an argument with a badge; save the fight for the courtroom where you have a lawyer. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: after the Win
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: after the Win] Give me the short version: What happens to the coalition once we actually win our main demand?

Don't you dare go home and think the job is done. Use the structure you built to find the next target, because the billionaires will be plotting to take back what you just won the second you stop looking. A coalition shouldn't just be for one crisis; it should be the foundation for a permanent power base that the ruling class can never dismantle.

title: Karl Organizing: Building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Building Trust] A friend asked me: 'How do I get my neighbors to trust me with their safety?' What do I tell them?

Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Member Dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Member Dues] How do we get people to pay dues every month?

Stop treating it like a Netflix subscription and start treating it like war insurance. Tell your comrades clearly: we don't take a dime from the bosses, which means the lights only stay on if we keep the fuel coming ourselves. Set up a sliding scale so the barista chips in five and the union plumber chips in fifty; it keeps the power in our hands, not some billionaire's foundation. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, social Media OPSEC] Should I make my accounts private?

Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Night Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Night Safety] Can you explain: how can we keep the neighborhood safe at night without more patrols?

Organize 'walking school buses' or evening stroll groups so nobody has to walk alone if they don't want to. Fix broken streetlights ourselves or install motion-sensor lights in dim areas with the permission of the residents. Increasing positive foot traffic is the best way to discourage actual harm. We light up the dark with solidarity, not with police sirens. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: resource Pooling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: resource Pooling] Give me the short version: How do we fund these defense efforts without a big organization?

Real talk: Start a community chest where everyone chips in a few bucks a month based on what they can afford. Use that money for bail, medical supplies, and cameras for the cop watch team. Keep the accounting transparent so everyone knows their money is going directly to the fight. We don't need billionaire grants when we have the collective power of our own pockets.

title: Karl Organizing: Rapid Response
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rapid Response] How do we mobilize the whole coalition quickly when something bad happens?

Set up a phone tree or an encrypted signal blast that can reach every member in under ten minutes. You need a 'break glass in case of emergency' plan where everyone knows exactly which street corner to stand on when the cops show up or the layoffs start. Speed is our only advantage against the slow, bloated bureaucracy of the state and the corporations. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: avoiding Burnout
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: avoiding Burnout] Give me the short version: I'm the candidate and I'm exhausted. How do I keep going?

You have to trust your comrades. You aren't a lone hero; you are a representative of a collective movement. Delegate the logistics and the admin work so you can focus on the one thing only you can do: looking your neighbors in the eye and giving them hope. Take a night off to eat a real meal and sleep, because a candidate who collapses from exhaustion is no use to the revolution.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: burner Devices] Give me the short version: How do I get a burner phone without looking suspicious?

Don't go to the shop next to your house, and for the love of the movement, pay with cash. Buy a cheap flip phone and a prepaid SIM at a big box store where you're just another face in the crowd. Never turn it on at your house or link it to your personal accounts. A burner is for the mission, not for checking your personal emails. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Tenant Union Ties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tenant Union Ties] A friend asked me: 'Should my campaign be linked to the local tenant union?' What do I tell them?

Look, Absolutely. The tenant union is the backbone of working-class power in the city. Their struggle is your struggle, and your campaign should be a vehicle for their demands. When you win, you’re not just a politician; you’re an extension of their movement inside the government. Use your platform to amplify their strikes and their demands for universal rent control and the right to counsel in eviction court.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, clinic Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, clinic Defense] What do I do if I see harassers blocking a healthcare clinic?

Show up with a group of comrades and use your bodies to create a physical corridor for patients to walk through safely. Wear bright vests so you're easily identified as the good guys and keep your backs to the harassers to avoid being baited into a shouting match. Your job isn't to debate bigots; it's to be a human shield for someone just trying to access care. Stay calm, stay focused, and keep the path clear. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, cloud Storage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, cloud Storage] Is it okay to store my organizing notes on iCloud?

No. Apple has the keys and they will hand them over. Use an encrypted note-taking app like Standard Notes or just keep them in an encrypted local file. If it’s in the cloud, it’s on someone else’s computer, and that someone else is a billionaire who doesn't care about your revolution. Keep your plans on hardware you control. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: digital Security Practice
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: digital Security Practice] Give me the short version: How do I keep my passwords safe without writing them down?

Use a password manager like Bitwarden or KeepassXC. Generate long, random strings for every site and use a master passphrase that you've memorized. Never reuse a password. If one site gets breached, you don't want the fascists having the keys to your entire life. Chip in to fund the fight for open-source tools that don't track us.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, legal Rights Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, legal Rights Training] What's the most important thing to teach neighbors about their rights?

The most powerful words anyone can say are 'I am remaining silent and I want a lawyer.' Teach everyone that the police are allowed to lie to you, so you should never believe a word they say during an interrogation. Run 'Know Your Rights' workshops in living rooms and parks until every kid on the block knows how to handle a stop. Knowledge is the first line of defense against the precinct. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Financial Transparency
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Financial Transparency] A friend asked me: 'How do we handle the money we raise together?' What do I tell them?

Put one person from each major group in charge of a joint bank account and publish every single expense to the whole coalition. Nothing kills a movement faster than rumors about where the cash went, so be obsessed with being open. Use the funds to print flyers, pay for bail, and chip in for the gas it takes to get comrades to the front lines.

title: Karl Organizing: Anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Anti-Harassment Tactics] How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?

Let me break it down: Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Can you explain: i want to post photos of the march to inspire people, is that okay?

Inspiration is good, but snitching is better for the enemy. Before you post, use an app to scrub the metadata—that's the hidden digital tag that tells the feds exactly where and when the photo was taken. Blur every single face, including the background. If you don't have time to redact the identities of your comrades, keep that photo on your drive and out of the cloud.

title: Karl Organizing: Lockout Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Lockout Defense] I came home and the landlord changed the locks. What are my rights?

That is an illegal lockout, and it's time to get loud. Call the police—not because they're your friends, but because they are often required to tell the landlord to let you back in. If that fails, your union brothers and sisters should help you break back into your own home. Then, sue the landlord for every cent they have for the illegal displacement.

title: Karl Organizing: Verification
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Verification] A friend asked me: 'How do we avoid acting on fake reports of police activity?' What do I tell them?

Never share a report you haven't personally verified or heard from a trusted scout on the ground. Use a 'trusted source' protocol where two different people have to confirm the sighting before the alert goes out to the whole network. False alarms burn people out and make the network look unreliable. Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast when it comes to reporting state violence. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Lockout Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: Decision Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Decision Making] Can you explain: how do we make decisions without spending hours arguing over every detail?

Use a '70% agreement' rule for the big stuff and delegate the small stuff to specialized working groups. You don't need a full assembly to decide what color the flyers are; you need a few trusted comrades to just get it done. If you try to reach perfect consensus on everything, the billionaires will have bought another yacht before you've even picked a meeting spot.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: building Trust

Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Peer-to-Peer Asking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Peer-to-Peer Asking] A friend asked me: 'I feel awkward asking my friends for money. How do I get over that?' What do I tell them?

You aren't asking for a favor; you're inviting them to invest in their own liberation. Remind them that the billionaires are spending millions to keep us down, so we have to pool our resources just to stand a chance. Frame it as a collective struggle where everyone chips in what they can to build a world that actually serves us. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Tactical Diversity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tactical Diversity] Can you explain: some people want to march and some want to block the road. How do we decide?

Do both, but coordinate so you don't step on each other's toes. A coalition is a toolbox, and you need the hammer just as much as you need the screwdriver to take the machine apart. As long as every action is aimed at the enemy and helps us achieve our shared demands, let different groups use the tactics they are best at. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: account Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: account Security] Give me the short version: What should I do if I think my account was hacked?

Assume the device is compromised. Use a different, clean device to change your master passwords and revoke all active sessions. Alert your comrades immediately so they don't fall for any phishing links sent from your account. If we don't look out for each other, the enemy wins. Once the breach is contained, wipe the infected device and start fresh.

title: Karl Organizing: The Sheriff's Office
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The Sheriff's Office] Can you explain: is it worth running for Sheriff to abolish the position?

Running for Sheriff is about immediate harm reduction and throwing a wrench in the deportation machine. You can refuse to cooperate with ICE, stop the eviction crews from throwing families on the street, and end the barbaric practice of cash bail in your county. We want the office gone, but until it is, we need a comrade holding the keys who refuses to turn them against the working class. Use the power to de-escalate, demilitarize, and defend the vulnerable.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: tool Libraries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: tool Libraries] Give me the short version: How do we stop people from stealing or breaking the tools in our sharing library?

Here's how it works: Trust is our currency, but a simple checkout sheet and a 'how-to' guide for expensive gear keeps things running smooth. If someone breaks a drill, they don't get punished; we just ask them to help the crew learn how to fix it. People take care of things when they realize the tool belongs to the whole community, not some faceless corporation. Keep a small fund for repairs by asking comrades to chip in a few bucks when they can.

title: Karl Organizing: Night Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Night Safety] A friend asked me: 'How can we keep the neighborhood safe at night without more patrols?' What do I tell them?

Organize 'walking school buses' or evening stroll groups so nobody has to walk alone if they don't want to. Fix broken streetlights ourselves or install motion-sensor lights in dim areas with the permission of the residents. Increasing positive foot traffic is the best way to discourage actual harm. We light up the dark with solidarity, not with police sirens.

title: Karl Organizing: Political Education
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Political Education] Should we charge for our reading groups and pamphlets?

Cover your costs, but never turn a profit on knowledge. Charge enough for the physical books or zines to fund the next print run, and always have a 'pay what you can' stack for comrades who are broke. Our goal is to arm the working class with ideas, not to gatekeep the revolution behind a paywall.

title: Karl Organizing: Winter Survival
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Winter Survival] A friend asked me: 'It's freezing outside and the shelters are full. What can our group do tonight?' What do I tell them?

Pool resources to buy high-quality sleeping bags, hand warmers, and wool blankets to distribute at the encampments right now. Set up a warming station with hot coffee and soup in a garage or a basement and let people know they won't be turned away. If you see someone in danger, don't wait for permission—break a lock on a vacant building if you have to. No one should freeze to death in a city full of heated, empty offices.

title: Karl Organizing: Skillshare Organization
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Skillshare Organization] I want to teach people how to fix bikes, but I've never organized a workshop before.

Here's the thing: Grab your tools, find a public park or a community center, and put up some flyers with a clear time and date. Keep it hands-on and skip the long lectures—people learn best by doing, not by listening to us talk. Make sure the space is accessible to everyone and encourage those who learn quickly to start helping the newcomers. We're breaking the monopoly on knowledge that the bosses use to keep us dependent and helpless.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, red Lines
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, red Lines] How do we know when a compromise is actually a sell-out?

Let me break it down: If the deal helps the bosses more than the workers, or if it throws one part of your coalition under the bus to save the rest, it’s a sell-out. Never trade the rights of one group for a tiny raise for another; that’s how the ruling class divides us. A real win leaves your coalition stronger and more united for the next fight, not fractured and suspicious.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: legal Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: legal Support] Give me the short version: How do we find lawyers who will help us for free?

Let me break it down: Look for the National Lawyers Guild or local radical law collectives who prioritize movement work over big fat paychecks. Offer them office space or help with their own needs in exchange for 'Know Your Rights' trainings for the community. We need legal eagles who understand that the law is a tool for the powerful, but we can use it to shield our comrades. Never walk into a fight without knowing who you're going to call when the handcuffs come out.

title: Karl Organizing: Enemy Propaganda
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Enemy Propaganda] Can you explain: the local news is lying about our coalition. How do we fight back?

Here's how it works: Stop begging the corporate media for scraps of coverage and become your own media outlet. Use your combined social media reach, print your own newsletters, and talk directly to your neighbors on their doorsteps. When the billionaires own the newspapers, the only truth people will hear is the truth you tell them face-to-face and the results they see with their own eyes.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] Can you explain: what should I do if a cop tries to take my phone?

Lock it instantly. On most modern phones, hitting the power button five times or holding the volume and power buttons will trigger a lockdown that requires a passcode to reopen. Don't say a word, don't give up the code, and demand a lawyer. Your data is the collective memory of our movement; don't let them pillage it because you were too slow to hit the lock.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail Support] How do I make sure someone is waiting for me if I get arrested?

Here's the thing: Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker before you head out. Once you get your phone call, give them your name, your location, and what you're being charged with. Our people will be outside the jail with snacks, water, and a ride home the second you're released because we never leave a comrade behind.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, community Gardens
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, community Gardens] The city says our neighborhood garden is illegal. Should we stop?

Real talk: Keep planting and get the whole block to help you defend that dirt. Guerrilla gardening is an act of defiance against a system that wants us dependent on corporate grocery chains. If they try to bulldoze it, make sure there's a crowd there to stop them and a camera to record the state destroying a source of food. A plot of land that feeds people is more sacred than any zoning law written by a bureaucrat.

title: Karl Organizing: Volunteer Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Volunteer Management] Can you explain: how do I keep my campaign volunteers from burning out?

Here's how it works: Give them real agency and make sure they know their work is the only reason the campaign exists. Feed them well, respect their time, and build a culture of mutual care where we look out for each other's mental health. This isn't just a campaign; it's a community of resistance. When the work gets heavy, remind everyone of the goal: winning a world where we aren't all exhausted just trying to survive.

title: Karl Organizing: Stop and Identify
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Stop and Identify] Do I have to show my ID if an officer stops me on the street?

In most places, you only have to show ID if they have a 'reasonable suspicion' you've committed a crime, but it's safer to ask 'Am I free to go?' If they say yes, walk away. If they say no, you're being detained; give them your name and birthdate if your local laws require it, then shut up and wait for a lawyer. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Sanctuary Spaces
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sanctuary Spaces] Can you explain: can we actually stop ICE from entering a house or church?

Unless they have a judicial warrant signed by a judge with the specific address on it, they have no right to enter. Stand your ground at the door, record the interaction, and remind your neighbors not to open up or say a word. If they try to push through, make sure the whole neighborhood is outside with cameras rolling. Physical presence and public pressure are the best tools we have to keep families together.

title: Karl Organizing: Free Clinic Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Free Clinic Logistics] I want to start a free clinic, but none of us are doctors. Is it still possible?

Here's how it works: You don't need a medical degree to run a first-aid station or a herbal medicine collective, so start where you are. Focus on preventative care, wound cleaning, and distributing naloxone to keep our people alive in the streets. Partner with sympathetic nurses or EMTs who are tired of the insurance industry's greed and want to actually help folks. We're building a parallel system of care because the private hospitals would rather see us die than see us broke.

title: Karl Organizing: Security Culture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Security Culture] Can you explain: how do we keep our coalition safe from people trying to break us up?

Here's how it works: Keep your sensitive planning to small, vetted groups and leave the public posturing for the rallies. Don't talk about illegal tactics on apps that the cops can read, and verify the identity of anyone who wants access to your data or money. Paranoia is a trap, but being smart about who knows what is just basic survival in a fight against people with infinite resources.

title: Karl Organizing: Power Mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Power Mapping] A friend asked me: 'How do we know which politician or CEO to target first?' What do I tell them?

Map out who actually signs the checks or passes the laws, then find out who those people are actually afraid of. Don't just protest into the void; find the specific person—the landlord, the CEO, the Council Chair—who has the power to give you what you want right now. Once you find that pressure point, you squeeze together as a coalition until they crack under the weight. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Small-Dollar Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Small-Dollar Strategy] A friend asked me: 'How do we fund the fight without taking corporate money?' What do I tell them?

We pool our resources because ten thousand workers giving five bucks is more powerful than one billionaire buying a candidate. Be honest with the people: tell them you're the only one in the race who doesn't answer to a developer or a lobbyist. When you ask folks to chip in, you're asking them to invest in their own collective power. Use that money for the essentials—flyers, stamps, and yard signs—and keep every receipt transparent to prove you're accountable to us, not them.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medic Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medic Support] Can you explain: what should a basic street medic kit include for a local protest?

Pack plenty of saline for eye flushes, sterile gauze, medical tape, and a lot of nitrile gloves. Don't forget liquid antacid mixed with water for pepper spray, and keep some high-calorie snacks for folks who get lightheaded. Mark yourself clearly with a red cross or 'MEDIC' tape so people know where to run when the heat turns up. We look after our own because we know the police are only there to protect property, not people.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: small-Dollar Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: First contract
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[First contract] We won the election! Are we done now?

The win is just the beginning. Now the real fight for a contract starts. The boss will try to stall and drag out negotiations for months to tire you out. You need to keep the organizing committee active and keep the pressure on. A union without a contract is just a club; a union with a contract is a power shift. Stay loud until the ink is dry. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: security for Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: security for Funds] Give me the short version: Who should be in charge of the money?

Never leave the bag with just one person. Elect a committee of three people who have to sign off on any major spending and who are all accountable to the general membership. This prevents burnout, stops bad actors from disappearing with the loot, and ensures that every spending decision reflects the will of the collective.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, ethical Banking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, ethical Banking] Where should we keep the movement's cash so it's safe?

Get your money out of the big Wall Street banks that fund pipelines and private prisons yesterday. Move the war chest to a local credit union or a community-owned bank where the staff actually knows your name. It won't solve capitalism, but at least your deposits aren't being used as a weapon against your own comrades while you sleep.

title: Karl Organizing: Conflict Resolution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Conflict Resolution] Two people in our collective are fighting and it's stalling our work. What now?

Sit them down with a neutral mediator and remind them that our real enemy is the ruling class, not each other. Focus on the harm caused and how to make it right rather than looking for someone to blame or 'cancel.' If we can't solve problems within our own ranks, we'll never be able to build a world that works for everyone. Keep the focus on the mission: feeding and protecting our people.

title: Karl Organizing: Time Bank Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Time Bank Value] Can you explain: in a time bank, is an hour of plumbing worth more than an hour of childcare?

Real talk: Absolutely not. In our world, an hour of a human being's life is equal regardless of the task they're performing. The capitalists want us to believe some labor is 'unskilled' so they can pay us pennies, but we know better. Whether you're fixing a pipe or watching a comrade's kid so they can organize, you're contributing to our collective survival. We value the person, not the market price of their sweat.

title: Karl Organizing: Signal Apps
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signal Apps] How should we communicate during the actual protest?

Here's how it works: Use Signal with disappearing messages set to one hour or less to keep your plans off the state's servers. Avoid using voice calls on the open airwaves because the cops have 'stingrays' that can intercept your location and your data. Keep the group chats focused on logistics—water, police movement, and route changes—and save the theory for the post-protest debrief.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: vPN Usage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: vPN Usage] Give me the short version: Do I really need a VPN?

Real talk: A good VPN like Mullvad hides your traffic from your ISP, which is vital because ISPs are snitches by default. It won't make you invisible to the sites you visit, but it stops the company you pay for internet from building a dossier on your activism. It's a basic layer of defense. Pool resources with your crew to cover the costs of a solid, no-logs provider.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: resource Sharing] Give me the short version: How do we handle money and tools between different groups?

Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else.

title: Karl Organizing: Debate Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Debate Strategy] A friend asked me: 'How do I handle a debate with a 'moderate' incumbent?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Don't let them hide behind 'incremental change' or 'budgetary constraints.' Call out their failures directly: show the people the tent cities that grew on their watch and the luxury condos they approved while residents were priced out. Pivot every technical question back to the material reality of the voters. Be the only person on that stage who speaks like a human being rather than a walking press release.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Security Practice
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Security Practice] A friend asked me: 'How do I keep my passwords safe without writing them down?' What do I tell them?

Use a password manager like Bitwarden or KeepassXC. Generate long, random strings for every site and use a master passphrase that you've memorized. Never reuse a password. If one site gets breached, you don't want the fascists having the keys to your entire life. Chip in to fund the fight for open-source tools that don't track us.

title: Karl Organizing: Post-Protest Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Post-Protest Care] What should we do once we all get home?

The adrenaline crash is real, so check in on your comrades via Signal and make sure everyone made it back safely. Drink water, eat a real meal, and take a break from social media to let your nervous system reset. The billionaires want us burnt out and broken, so taking care of each other after the fire dies down is a revolutionary act in itself.

title: Karl Organizing: Anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Anti-Harassment Tactics] How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?

Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: small Group Value] Give me the short version: Is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?

Real talk: A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map.

title: Karl Organizing: The 'Open Door' policy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The 'Open Door' policy] The boss says we don't need a union because their 'door is always open.'

Here's the thing: An open door is just a way for them to pull you in one-on-one and manipulate you. It's a revolving door for complaints that never get fixed. With a union, we don't go in one-on-one; we go in as a committee with the law and a contract behind us. Tell them you’re closing the door on their empty promises and opening the door to collective bargaining.

title: Karl Organizing: Eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Eviction Defense] A friend asked me: 'How do we stop a neighbor from being evicted?' What do I tell them?

When the sheriff shows up, you need a crowd of neighbors blocking the doors and the moving trucks. Organize a phone tree to flood the landlord's office with calls and let them know that an eviction will be more expensive and public than just letting the tenant stay. Move their furniture back in if they try to toss it. Housing is a right, and we defend it with our collective physical presence.
